  "text": "“Don’t touch it,” Ada said.

The constable’s hand hovered above the boards. Beyond the yellow door, the small palm remained open, patient as a beggar’s.

“It’s Mara,” he whispered.

Ada held up the ring. “Then ask her something only she knew.”

His mouth worked. The black line crept past his collar, dividing his throat. “What did you call the dog?”

The hand curled. Three knocks sounded against the door, then two.

“That isn’t an answer,” Elias said.

“It’s the only one she ever gave me.” The constable’s eyes filled. “The dog had no name. She said he could choose one when he was older.”

The hand reached farther into the room. Its nails left sooty marks on the threshold. Ada saw then that it cast no shadow. The shadow lay behind the constable, stretched from his pinned hand to the open door.

“Venn,” she said, “move his heel.”

Venn braced against Elias and kicked the stone. It shifted. The last groove of OPEN slipped beneath the constable’s boot, and the door jolted against its frame. The small hand seized the edge before it could shut.

The constable cried out. The line around his neck tightened, pulling his head toward the gap.

Ada drove the ring into the groove where the missing letter had been. Metal struck stone. From behind the door came a child’s sharp gasp.

The hand vanished. The line fell from the constable like a length of burnt string, and the yellow door closed.

For a moment, no one moved. Then three knocks came from beneath the floor, followed by two."
